name: Annapoorna Dining Hall (Temple Annadana)
signature_dish: Free sattvic pilgrim meal on plantain leaf
why_it_matters: The Annapoorna Dining Hall beside the Sri Manjunatha Swamy Temple — one of the largest free-meal operations in India, serving over 50,000 devotees a day. The modernised hall and mechanised kitchen, unveiled by Dr Veerendra Heggade in 1986, have been featured on National Geographic for their scale, cleanliness and architecture. Free annadana to every visitor is the spiritual heart of Dharmasthala.
insider_tip: Lunch runs roughly 11am-2.30pm with separate Sunday-Monday timings; you sit on the floor and the meal — rice, sambar, two curries, a palya, curd rice and a sweet — is served on a leaf. Come early in the session to avoid the longest queues. No charge of any kind.
signature_address: Annapoorna Dining Hall, Sri Manjunatha Swamy Temple, Dharmasthala, Belthangady Taluk, Dakshina Kannada District, Karnataka 574216

name: Laxmi Prasanna
area: Main road, near temple arch, Dharmasthala
why_it_matters: A pure-veg restaurant on the main road, right by the arch as you enter the temple complex — the most-cited paid sit-down option in Dharmasthala for pilgrims who want a quick private meal or breakfast outside the annadana timings. Reviewers note good service and local cuisine.
insider_tip: Handy when the free hall is between sessions or you want an early breakfast before darshan. Standard South Indian tiffin and meals; like everywhere in town it is strictly pure-veg, no alcohol. Cash and UPI.
signature_address: Laxmi Prasanna, main road, near temple arch, Dharmasthala, Belthangady Taluk, Dakshina Kannada District, Karnataka 574216

name: Aditya View Hotel Veg Restaurant
signature_dish: Pure-veg South and North Indian meals
why_it_matters: The pure-veg restaurant at Hotel Aditya View near the Kumaradhara River at Nidle — a more comfortable hotel-attached dining option in a town where most eating happens at the free hall. Serves South Indian, North Indian and local Karnataka dishes.
insider_tip: Better suited to travellers staying out near the river than to a quick post-darshan bite in the bazaar. Standard hotel veg menu — South Indian tiffin is the safest order. Cards, UPI and cash.
signature_address: Aditya View Hotel & Veg Restaurant, Nidle, near Kumaradhara River, Dharmasthala, Belthangady Taluk, Dakshina Kannada District, Karnataka 574216
